concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bound on growth of a running time.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of coefficients times powers of a variable, with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi, with roots of unity as the unit-modulus examples.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A finite-state machine with finite alphabet and several one-dimensional tapes, each head moving at most one cell per step.

concepts.name: Multiplication history and the n log n conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage–Strassen multiplied n-bit integers in O(n log n log log n) and conjectured n log n optimal; Harvey–van der Hoeven reached O(n log n).

evidence.quote:
Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper
bound
proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Convolution and multiplication
concepts.gloss: Multiplying integers by splitting into radix digits reduces to convolving short integer coefficient lists, i.e. multiplying polynomials.

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: Evaluating a coefficient list at powers of a primitive root of unity; it turns cyclic convolution into pointwise products.

evidence.quote:
it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for
this convolution

concepts.name: FFT and two-point butterflies
concepts.gloss: Fast Fourier transform levels built from address rearrangements, root multiplications and two-point butterfly operations; each of Θ(log n) levels scanning Θ(n) bits costs Θ(n log n).

evidence.quote:
the transform calculation consists of address
rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials, whose powers act as roots of unity.

symbols.name: ring size
symbols.meaning: The number of coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: Polynomials in y with complex coefficients reduced using y^r = -1; powers of y are roots of unity and multiplying by one is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote:
one coordinate
is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Nussbaumer-style transforms over the polynomial ring where roots of unity are powers of y, so root multiplication is a signed shift.

evidence.quote:
These are the
synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and
Nussbaumer

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Exact polynomial products are computed by packing signed coefficients into one long integer and calling the established O(n log n) multiplier as an ordinary subroutine.

evidence.quote:
Signed coefficient
packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Prime cyclic axes and the Chinese remainder map
concepts.gloss: The coefficient list is placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map preserving convolution.

evidence.quote:
the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of
distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves
convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven technique expressing a Fourier transform through a multidimensional transform whose axis lengths are powers of two.

evidence.quote:
Gaussian
resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a
power-of-two tensor transform.

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Converts a transform of arbitrary length into a cyclic convolution via multiplication by chirp phases.

evidence.quote:
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,
including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Last-coordinate phase twist
concepts.gloss: A phase twist turns the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo y^r+1, whose negative wrap yields the original cyclic wrap after untwisting.

evidence.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Fixed-point precision and exact recovery
concepts.gloss: Records hold complex fixed-point coefficients; Gaussian dyadics are exact, one truncation follows a contractive layer, and the final error is below 1/2 so rounding and carries give the exact product.

evidence.quote:
Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics,
whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.

proves that the recovered
coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$

concepts.name: Tape arrays, scans and elementary streams
concepts.gloss: Arrays stored in address order on tapes with scans, controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings costing linear time.

evidence.quote:
We distinguish moving one
digit in a fixed radix, which needs a bounded number of scans, from
interchanging fields whose numbers of digits grow.

concepts.name: Fast interchange of address fields
concepts.gloss: Swapping two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in a Cartesian-product array in O(V u^τ) time, τ<1, using intermediate XOR combinations that end in an exact permutation.

evidence.quote: Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

concepts.name: Address shear and triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: The endpoint operator (H,D)->(H+D,D) on address fields, with rank reduction via lower-triangular (Bruhat) factorization.

evidence.quote:
Two further linear-cost address
updates complete their interchange.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: Applying H0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) coefficientwise on the same selected bit of up to d address chunks, in O(V d^λ') time with λ'<1.

evidence.quote: simultaneously on selected coordinate bits of the numerical arrays

concepts.name: Linear networks, roles and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network exchanges banks of values with signs and restores auxiliary values; rows are spread over roles and each vertex stores D_v g in an invertible linear frame so intermediate frames cancel.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame
A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.

concepts.name: Finite networks from three-element subsets
concepts.gloss: Fixed networks with nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from three-element subset intersections, giving s<Wm smaller calls.

evidence.quote:
The decisive property is that the total
number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.name: Recursive power saving
concepts.gloss: Calling a parameter-mf operation as s calls at parameter f on volume V/W raises normalized cost by s/W<m per multiplication of the parameter by m, yielding a power saving.

evidence.quote:
This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Resampling with permutations retained in the transform
concepts.gloss: Source and target coordinate permutations stay in the transform identity and cancel across forward, pointwise, and inverse transforms instead of being executed as sorts.

evidence.quote:
Section~\ref{sec:resampling} retains the
source and target coordinate permutations in the transform identity

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits of each input integer.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^-182 giving the power saving in the logarithm.

concepts.gloss: A deterministic fixed-tape machine multiplies n-bit integers in O(n(lg n)^(1−κ)) time, κ=2^−182, disproving the n log n conjecture in this model; chain: digit convolution, prime axes, resampling and chirps, polynomial ring transforms with fast tape procedures, then rounding and carries.

evidence.quote:
computes this exact product for every $n\ge1$ and every pair of $n$-bit
inputs.

concepts.name: Recurrences and divide and conquer
concepts.gloss: A problem of size N is solved by recursive calls on smaller pieces plus combining work, and the total cost is found by solving the resulting recurrence.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where numbers are identified when they differ by a multiple of a modulus.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Primes are integers greater than 1 with no proper divisors, and coprime integers share no common factor other than 1.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, residues modulo each one determine a unique residue modulo their product.

concepts.name: Binary representation and bit operations
concepts.gloss: Integers are written as strings of bits, with bitwise XOR and carry propagation in addition.

concepts.name: Radix (base) expansion
concepts.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a base.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of a finite set of positions.

concepts.name: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension
concepts.gloss: Sets closed under linear combinations, described by a basis, with dimension the basis size.

concepts.name: Finite field F_2
concepts.gloss: The two-element field where addition is XOR and multiplication is AND.

concepts.name: Matrices, rank and invertibility
concepts.gloss: Linear maps are represented by matrices that compose by multiplication; invertible ones have an inverse and rank counts independent rows.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.gloss: Row operations reduce a matrix to triangular form, giving factorizations into triangular pieces.

concepts.name: Cartesian product of sets
concepts.gloss: The set of tuples with each coordinate drawn from its own set, used to index multidimensional arrays.

concepts.name: Cyclic groups and roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The integers mod n under addition form a cyclic group, and the n-th roots of unity are the complex solutions of z^n = 1.

concepts.name: Real and complex analysis basics
concepts.gloss: Absolute values and norms of real and complex numbers, the triangle inequality, and elementary functions such as exp.

concepts.name: Rounding, floor and ceiling
concepts.gloss: Floor, ceiling and nearest-integer maps from reals to integers.

concepts.name: Logarithms and exponents
concepts.gloss: The base-2 logarithm and the arithmetic of exponents and powers of two.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and Karatsuba
concepts.gloss: The standard quadratic digit-by-digit multiplication and its divide and conquer speedup.

concepts.name: Sorting and merging
concepts.gloss: Ordering records by key, with comparison sorting costing O(N log N).

concepts.name: Pigeonhole principle and counting arguments
concepts.gloss: Elementary counting tools for finite sets, subsets and their sizes.

concepts.name: Lower and upper bound asymptotics
concepts.gloss: Theta, Omega and little-o relate growth rates of functions alongside big-O.

concepts.name: Constants and parameters in complexity bounds
concepts.gloss: Fixed constants hidden in big-O and powers of log n as polylogarithmic factors.

background.summary: An undergraduate computer science reader who has studied algorithms and data structures (divide and conquer, recurrences, sorting, basic complexity), discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, binary representation, sets, permutations, induction), and linear algebra (vector spaces, subspaces, dimension, rank, invertible matrices, Gaussian elimination, triangular matrices) at an introductory level. They know the basics of Fourier analysis and probability/real analysis only as far as complex numbers and elementary calculus. They have not studied algebraic number theory, advanced finite-field theory, Lie groups or specialist FFT/multiplication literature.
